summary: Bumps the exact @cipherstash/protect-ffi pin from 0.30.0 to 0.31.0 (a breaking upstream release) in @cipherstash/stack and adapts stack to it: error-code detection moves from `instanceof ProtectError` to a value check (`isProtectErrorCode`), which also changes DynamoDB `handleError` to stop passing foreign codes through; the wasm-inline `newClient` call moves credentials into `clientOpts`, renames `strategy` to `authStrategy` and stops pre-normalising `cast_as`; bulk/model payloads stop forwarding the correlation `id` across the FFI. A CI step now fails fast on a non-hex CS_CLIENT_KEY and a major changeset documents that an explicit clientKey must now be hex. I checked every native and wasm FFI call site at head and none still forwards an `id` or other undeclared key. The main residual risks sit in the dependency boundary, which could not be inspected: the native `newClient` call still passes the auth strategy under the old top-level `strategy` name (only a mocked test covers it), customers with base64 client keys will fail at construction on upgrade (loud, documented, major bump), and the wasm entry now relies on the FFI's own cast_as normalisation. No CI results were supplied and no tests could be run, so the verdict is advisory pending the credentialed suites.

behaviour_changes.description: @cipherstash/stack now pins @cipherstash/protect-ffi exactly at 0.31.0 (was 0.30.0); stack-drizzle and stack-supabase devDependencies follow. Upgrading stack forces the new native/wasm binding on customers.

An explicitly supplied clientKey (config.clientKey / CS_CLIENT_KEY) must now be hex; base64 values that previously worked are rejected at client construction. The change comes from the dependency; stack documents it as a major release.

wasm-inline Encryption() now calls newClient with { authStrategy, encryptConfig, clientOpts: { clientId, clientKey }, eqlVersion: 3 }, no longer pre-normalises cast_as via normalizeCastAs, and drops the `as never` cast so the call is type-checked.

getErrorCode and DynamoDB handleError now recognise an FFI error by checking the `code` value against protect-ffi's known set rather than `instanceof ProtectError` / any string `code`. Non-FFI codes (e.g. ECONNRESET) now map to undefined / DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR; plain Errors carrying a valid FFI code are now recognised.
Bulk encrypt/decrypt and model helpers strip the stack-side correlation `id` before calling encryptBulk/decryptBulk(Fallible). Results remain correlated positionally.
The shared require-cs-secrets composite action gains a step that fails the job when CS_CLIENT_KEY is not an even-length hex string; it is used by every credentialed workflow.
The bundled stash-auth agent skill (shipped to customers) gains guidance that CS_CLIENT_KEY must be hex and how to recover on native vs wasm-inline entries.

failure_scenarios.title: Native client auth strategy passed under pre-0.31 `strategy` key
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer constructs the native Encryption client with config.authStrategy (e.g. an OidcFederationStrategy for user-scoped access) on 0.31.0.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The wasm call was moved to `authStrategy` because 0.31 renamed the field (E-5), but the native call at encryption/index.ts still passes `strategy: config.authStrategy` at the top level (E-2). The only test is mocked and asserts `opts.strategy` (E-3), so it cannot show what the real 0.31 Neon entry does with it. A test comment says `strategy` survives as a deprecated alias on the wasm side (E-4); that is an unverified author claim, and the native side is not covered by it.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If 0.31 ignores the old key, the client silently falls back to the default `auto` strategy and authenticates with ambient credentials instead of the end-user's federated identity, so operations stop being bound to that identity. If 0.31 rejects it, every native client using authStrategy fails at construction.

failure_scenarios.title: Customers with base64 clientKey fail at construction after upgrade
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer upgrades @cipherstash/stack while config.clientKey / CS_CLIENT_KEY holds the base64 spelling (e.g. copied from ~/.cipherstash/secretkey.json).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The exact pin forces protect-ffi 0.31.0 (E-1), which per the changeset decodes an explicit clientKey as hex only (E-9). On wasm-inline the clientKey is required config and there is no profile-store fallback (E-12).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Every encryption operation in that deployment fails at client construction with a deliberately terse message. The failure is loud and recoverable by re-encoding the key, but it is a full outage of encryption for that app until fixed.

existing_verification.description: require-cs-secrets now rejects a non-hex CS_CLIENT_KEY in this repo's CI (guards this repo's pipelines only, not customers).

missing_verification: No in-repo test of the hex-only rejection on the native or wasm entry (the behaviour lives in protect-ffi and was not inspectable).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Already mitigated by the major version bump, the changeset upgrade note, the stash-auth skill guidance and `stash env` emitting hex. Release notes should lead with this. Optionally, have stack detect a base64-looking key and return a ClientInitError naming the encoding, without echoing the key.

failure_scenarios.title: wasm encryptConfig now relies on FFI cast_as normalisation
failure_scenarios.trigger: A wasm-inline client encrypts or queries a column whose SDK cast_as the 0.31 Rust normaliser maps differently from stack's toEqlCastAs (e.g. 'number' -> 'double', 'json' -> 'jsonb').
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Base ran normalizeCastAs(encryptConfig) before newClient (E-6), so wasm used stack's mapping (E-7). Head forwards the SDK spelling unnormalised (E-5, E-8) and depends on 0.31's Rust-side mapping, which could not be inspected.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If a mapping diverged, wasm-written ciphertexts or query terms for that type would be encoded under a different cast than existing data and native-written terms. Range/equality queries could then silently miss rows, or decryption could return a differently typed plaintext.

existing_verification.description: wasm-inline-new-client.test.ts / wasm-inline-v3.test.ts assert cast_as 'string' is forwarded unchanged, against a mocked binding.
The native entry already passed un-normalised config to the FFI at base, so the FFI mapping is already in production use for native clients.

missing_verification: A wasm round-trip/cross-binding test per cast_as variant on 0.31 (wasm encrypt -> native decrypt/query and the reverse).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Run the credentialed wasm integration suites (v2-decrypt-compat, v3 matrix) on 0.31 before release, or add a unit test that pins the FFI's canonical cast for each SDK variant to toEqlCastAs.

failure_scenarios.title: DynamoDB callers branching on error.code see a different code
failure_scenarios.trigger: An application using the DynamoDB helpers branches on EncryptedDynamoDBError.code for an error whose code is not in protect-ffi's set.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: handleError now keeps a code only if isProtectErrorCode accepts it, otherwise it returns DYNAMODB_ENCRYPTION_ERROR (E-13). Before, any string code passed through.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Retry-vs-fail logic keyed on transport codes such as ECONNRESET stops matching, so the caller may stop retrying transient errors. The impact is limited to error routing and recoverable.
